title: SQL Injection
description: SQL injection via string concatenation or f-string interpolation in database queries. User input embedded directly into SQL without parameterization allows UNION attacks, data exfiltration, authentication bypass, and arbitrary UPDATE or DELETE. Common patterns: execute('SELECT ... WHERE id=' + user_input), f-string SQL, %s-formatting outside parameterized call.
remediation: Use parameterized queries: conn.execute('SELECT ... WHERE id=?', (user_input,))

title: SQL Injection via Hibernate
description: ORM-level SQL injection when raw HQL or native SQL queries are constructed with user input instead of named parameters.
remediation: Use named parameters in ORM queries

title: OS Command Injection
description: User-controlled input passed to os.system(), subprocess.call(), subprocess.Popen() with shell=True, or os.popen() enables arbitrary shell command execution. An attacker can run rm -rf, exfiltrate data, or pivot to internal systems.
remediation: Use subprocess with a list of arguments and shell=False; never pass user input to shell=True

title: Code Injection via eval or exec
description: Calling eval() or exec() with user-controlled or external input allows arbitrary Python code execution. Template systems using eval for expression evaluation (e.g. {{ user_expr }}) are vulnerable to Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) enabling RCE.
remediation: Replace eval() with a safe expression evaluator; for templates use Jinja2 with SandboxedEnvironment

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data (pickle)
description: pickle.loads(), marshal.loads(), or yaml.load() called with untrusted or unverified input enables arbitrary code execution during deserialization. An attacker crafts a payload that executes os.system() or reverse shell on the server. No signature validation = full RCE.
remediation: Use json.loads() for data interchange; if pickle is required, validate HMAC signature before deserializing

title: Path Traversal
description: User input used in file paths without sanitization allows reading or writing files outside the intended directory. Patterns: open(user_input), os.path.join(base, user_input) without canonicalization, send_file(filename).
remediation: Canonicalize paths with os.path.realpath() and verify the result starts with the allowed base directory

title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
description: User-supplied HTML or JavaScript inserted into responses without escaping allows attackers to execute scripts in victims' browsers, steal cookies, or perform actions on behalf of users.
remediation: HTML-escape all user input in templates; use Content-Security-Policy headers

title: Open Redirect
description: Redirect URL taken from user input without validation allows phishing attacks where the application redirects users to malicious sites.
remediation: Validate redirect URLs against an allowlist of trusted domains

title: Hardcoded Credentials
description: API keys, passwords, tokens, or secrets hardcoded in source code (e.g. STRIPE_SECRET = 'sk_live_...', JWT_SECRET = '...', ADMIN_TOKEN = '...'). Anyone with read access to the source or compiled artifact can extract and abuse the credentials.
remediation: Move secrets to environment variables (os.environ.get) or a secrets manager like AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault

title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Key
description: JWT secrets, encryption keys, or HMAC keys hardcoded directly in code. If the key leaks the entire authentication or encryption system is compromised. Common: JWT_SECRET = 'mysecret', AES_KEY = b'hardcodedkey...'
remediation: Load cryptographic keys from environment variables or a key management service; never commit keys to source control

title: Weak Cryptographic Algorithm (MD5/SHA1)
description: MD5 or SHA-1 used for password hashing or data integrity. MD5 is broken for cryptographic use — it can be cracked in seconds with rainbow tables or GPU attacks. hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest() for passwords is critically insecure.
remediation: Use bcrypt, argon2, or scrypt for passwords; use SHA-256 or SHA-3 for integrity checks

title: Insufficient Password Hashing
description: Passwords stored with fast hashing algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 without salt/work factor) are vulnerable to offline brute-force attacks. Fast hashes allow billions of guesses per second on modern hardware.
remediation: Use bcrypt (cost factor >= 12) or argon2id for all password storage

title: Insufficient Randomness
description: Using random.random() or random.randint() for security-sensitive purposes (tokens, session IDs, CSRF tokens) instead of secrets.token_hex() or os.urandom(). The Mersenne Twister PRNG is predictable.
remediation: Use secrets.token_hex(32) or os.urandom(32) for all security-sensitive random values

title: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
description: Passwords, API keys, PII, or sensitive configuration stored or transmitted in plaintext without encryption.
remediation: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit using AES-256-GCM or TLS 1.2+

title: Improper Authentication
description: Authentication checks that can be bypassed: reset_token accepted but never verified, password reset without validating the token exists in the database, authentication relying on client-supplied values without server-side verification.
remediation: Always verify reset tokens against a server-side store with expiry; never trust client-supplied identity claims

title: Unverified Password Change
description: Password reset or change endpoint that accepts a reset token parameter but does not validate it against a stored token. Allows any attacker to reset any user's password by supplying only the email address.
remediation: Validate reset token exists in password_reset_tokens table, matches the email, and has not expired before updating the password

title: Improper Access Control / IDOR
description: Insecure Direct Object Reference: endpoint accepts a user_id or resource_id parameter without verifying the authenticated user owns that resource. Allows enumeration of all users, orders, or records by iterating IDs.
remediation: Always verify ownership: WHERE id=? AND user_id=current_user_id; never expose sequential IDs

title: Improper Authorization
description: Role-based access checks missing or bypassable. Admin functions accessible without verifying the caller has admin role. Privilege escalation by modifying role parameter in request.
remediation: Enforce role checks server-side on every request; never trust user-supplied role claims

title: Observable Timing Discrepancy (Timing Attack)
description: Secret comparison using == or != operator leaks information through timing differences. Python string comparison is short-circuit: 'admin' == 'a...' exits early, measurable with microsecond-precision timing. Allows brute-force of tokens and passwords.
remediation: Use hmac.compare_digest(a, b) for all security-sensitive comparisons

title: Improper Restriction of Authentication Attempts
description: No rate limiting or account lockout on login, password reset, or token validation endpoints. Allows brute-force attacks against passwords and tokens.
remediation: Implement rate limiting (e.g. Flask-Limiter, slowapi) and progressive lockout after failed attempts

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
description: State-changing requests (POST, PUT, DELETE) not protected by CSRF tokens allow attackers to forge requests on behalf of authenticated users by tricking them into visiting a malicious page.
remediation: Use synchronizer token pattern or SameSite=Strict cookies; validate Origin and Referer headers

title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
description: Sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII) sent over HTTP instead of HTTPS, or logged in plaintext to log files or error messages.
remediation: Enforce HTTPS everywhere; never log sensitive values; use structured logging with field-level redaction

title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (ReDoS)
description: Regular expressions with exponential backtracking applied to user-controlled input. Crafted input can cause regex evaluation to take seconds or minutes, enabling Denial of Service.
remediation: Use non-backtracking regex engines or validate input length before regex application

title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits
description: Loading entire database tables or large files into memory without pagination or streaming. Can cause Out-Of-Memory errors under load or with adversarial inputs.
remediation: Use pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET or cursor-based), streaming, or lazy evaluation for large datasets

title: N+1 Query Problem
description: Database query inside a loop: one query per item instead of a single batched query. For N items this creates N+1 database round-trips. At scale (1000+ items) this causes severe latency and database overload. Common pattern: for uid in user_ids: conn.execute('SELECT ... WHERE id=?', (uid,))
remediation: Replace per-item queries with a single IN-clause: SELECT ... WHERE id IN (?,?,?) and build a dict for O(1) lookups

title: O(n²) Nested Loop Algorithm
description: Nested loops iterating the same collection: for each element, iterating all elements again to find matches. Quadratic time complexity makes the function unusable at scale — 10000 items = 100M iterations.
remediation: Replace nested loops with a dict-based O(n) pass: group by key in one scan, then filter

title: String Concatenation in Loop
description: Building strings with += or + inside a loop creates O(n²) memory allocations because Python strings are immutable and each concatenation copies the entire string. For large inputs this causes severe performance degradation.
remediation: Collect parts in a list and join at the end: ''.join(parts) or ', '.join(items)

title: Linear Lookup in seen List
description: Using a list for deduplication or membership checking (if x in seen_list) causes O(n) per lookup, making the overall algorithm O(n²). Common in deduplication loops.
remediation: Replace the seen list with a set for O(1) membership checks

title: Improper Check or Handling of Exceptional Conditions
description: Bare except clauses, swallowing exceptions silently, or returning None/False on error instead of raising. Hides bugs, makes debugging impossible, and can allow partial state to persist.
remediation: Catch specific exception types; log and re-raise or return meaningful error responses

title: Missing Release of Resource After Effective Lifetime
description: Database connections, file handles, or network sockets opened but never closed. In long-running processes this causes connection pool exhaustion and resource leaks.
remediation: Use context managers (with sqlite3.connect(...) as conn) or explicit finally blocks to guarantee resource release

title: Improper Adherence to Coding Standards
description: Non-descriptive function or variable names (p, d, calc, r, n, t) that make code impossible to understand without execution context. Violates PEP8 and makes maintenance expensive.
remediation: Use descriptive names that reflect purpose: get_nested_value instead of p, compute_order_stats instead of calc

title: Use of Redundant Code
description: Duplicated logic (copy-paste code), duplicate database connection opening, or repeated computation that could be extracted into a helper function. Increases maintenance burden and risk of inconsistency.
remediation: Extract duplicated logic into a shared helper function; open shared resources once per call

title: Irrelevant Code
description: Dead code, commented-out blocks, unreachable branches, or unused imports that add noise and confusion without serving any purpose.
remediation: Remove dead code; use version control history to recover if needed

title: Insufficient Technical Documentation
description: Missing or inadequate docstrings on non-trivial public functions. Callers cannot understand parameters, return values, side effects, or error conditions without reading the implementation.
remediation: Add concise docstrings describing purpose, parameters, return value, and any side effects

title: Improper Following of Specification by Caller
description: Missing type hints on public functions makes static analysis impossible and forces callers to inspect implementation. Particularly harmful in larger codebases.
remediation: Add type annotations to all public function parameters and return types

title: Excessive Code Complexity
description: Functions with deep nesting (4+ levels), multiple unrelated responsibilities, or cyclomatic complexity above 10. Hard to test, maintain, and reason about.
remediation: Apply Single Responsibility Principle; extract nested conditions into guard clauses; split large functions

title: Hard-coded Password
description: Passwords, PINs, or passphrases written directly into source code. Common patterns: password = 'admin123', DB_PASSWORD = 'secret', API_KEY = 'sk_live_...'
remediation: Read passwords from environment variables or a secrets vault at runtime

title: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
description: Passwords, tokens, or PII stored in database columns, log files, or configuration files without encryption or hashing.
remediation: Hash passwords with bcrypt/argon2; encrypt PII at rest; exclude secrets from logs

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
description: User-controlled URL passed to requests.get(), urllib, or httpx without validation allows attackers to make the server fetch internal resources (AWS metadata endpoint, internal APIs, localhost services).
remediation: Validate URLs against an allowlist; block private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x)

title: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
description: Stack traces, SQL errors, or internal paths exposed in HTTP responses or logs reveal implementation details useful to attackers.
remediation: Return generic error messages to clients; log detailed errors server-side only with appropriate access controls

title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
description: Files, directories, or database records created with overly permissive access rights allow unauthorized read or write access.
remediation: Apply principle of least privilege; use chmod 600 for sensitive files; restrict database grants

title: Missing Authorization
description: Sensitive operations (admin actions, data modification, role changes) performed without verifying the caller has the necessary role or permission. Function accepts an admin_token but compares it with == instead of constant-time comparison, or skips verification entirely.
remediation: Enforce authorization on every sensitive operation; use hmac.compare_digest for token comparison

title: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
description: Webhook payloads, API responses, or serialized data accepted and processed without verifying a cryptographic signature. Allows injection of forged payloads.
remediation: Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature before processing any incoming payload; reject unsigned data

title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
description: Arithmetic on untrusted integer inputs without bounds checking can overflow, producing unexpected negative or zero values used in security decisions or memory allocation.
remediation: Validate integer inputs are within expected bounds before arithmetic operations

title: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
description: Authentication failures, privilege escalations, and suspicious inputs not logged. Without audit trails, breaches go undetected and post-incident investigation is impossible.
remediation: Log security events (auth failures, role changes, admin actions) with timestamp, user, and IP; set up alerting on anomalies

title: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
description: Functions inherently dangerous when used with untrusted input: eval(), exec(), pickle.loads(), yaml.load(), subprocess with shell=True, os.system(). These functions can execute arbitrary code.
remediation: Replace with safe alternatives: ast.literal_eval() for simple expressions, json.loads() for data, subprocess list form for commands

title: Inadequate Encryption Strength
description: Weak cipher choices: DES, 3DES, RC4, RSA-1024, AES-ECB mode. ECB mode in particular is deterministic and leaks patterns in encrypted data.
remediation: Use AES-256-GCM for symmetric encryption; RSA-2048+ or ECDSA P-256 for asymmetric; never use ECB mode
